# T-0079: Name the generated files

## What to build

A generated file repeated in a host makes every name it defines ambiguous (protobuf's Java, C# and C amalgamation entries in BACKLOG.md), and nothing names it.

A file is a generated file (GLOSSARY.md) when git's attributes mark it (`linguist-generated`) or when its header carries a known marker: protobuf's compiler ("Generated by the protocol buffer compiler.  DO NOT EDIT!"), Go's convention (`// Code generated ... DO NOT EDIT.` before the first code). The markers are data, beside each language's (ADR 0003). `check` and the report list the generated files, with the count of ambiguous calls their names take part in, and a ready `exclude` line. No link changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A file marked `linguist-generated` in `.gitattributes` is listed.
- [ ] A file with protobuf's or Go's header is listed; the same text below the first code is not.
- [ ] `check` and REPORT.md give the `exclude` line to paste.
- [ ] The graph's links are unchanged: the snapshots of T-0072 and T-0073 pass as they are.
- [ ] Measured on protobuf: which of its generated files are named, and whether upb's amalgamated files are (not verified so far); the numbers in BACKLOG.md's entries.
